title: Expand health assistant with full multi-specialty medical knowledge and summarized responses

requirements.summary: Expand specialtyKnowledgeBase.ts to include comprehensive, detailed entries for all 10 medical specialties with keywords, conditions, symptoms, diagnostic tools, treatments, red flags, and formatted content covering diagnosis, treatment, and prevention
acceptanceCriteria: All 10 specialties (cardiologist, dermatologist, pediatrician, surgeon, neurologist, general practitioner, anesthesiologist, oncologist, gynecologist, radiologist) have dedicated entries in specialtyKnowledgeBase.ts
Each entry covers diagnosis, treatment, and prevention aspects
Each entry includes at least 10 keywords for routing
Each entry includes red flags / emergency indicators

file_operations.description: Expand the specialty knowledge base to include comprehensive entries for all 10 medical specialties. Each specialty (cardiologist, dermatologist, pediatrician, surgeon, neurologist, general practitioner, anesthesiologist, oncologist, gynecologist, radiologist) must have: (1) at least 10 keywords for query routing, (2) arrays of common conditions, symptoms, diagnostic tools, and treatments, (3) red flags/emergency indicators array, (4) a detailed formatted content string with sections for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Ensure content is factual, informative, and includes appropriate medical disclaimers.

requirements.summary: Expand medicalKnowledgeBase.ts to include a broad set of conditions and topics across all 10 specialties, covering major conditions in cardiology, dermatology, pediatrics, surgery, neurology, general practice, anesthesiology, oncology, gynecology, and radiology
acceptanceCriteria: medicalKnowledgeBase.ts contains entries for major conditions across all 10 specialties
Each topic entry has relevant keywords and detailed markdown response content
Topics cover diagnosis, treatment options, and preventive measures

file_operations.description: Expand the medical knowledge base array to include comprehensive topic entries for major conditions across all 10 specialties. Add entries for: heart disease, arrhythmia, hypertension (cardiology); acne, eczema, psoriasis, skin cancer (dermatology); childhood illnesses, vaccinations, developmental milestones (pediatrics); pre/post-operative care, wound management (surgery); migraines, epilepsy, stroke, Parkinson's (neurology); common colds, chronic disease management, preventive care (general practice); anesthesia types, pain management, sedation (anesthesiology); cancer types, chemotherapy, immunotherapy (oncology); menstrual disorders, pregnancy, menopause (gynecology); imaging modalities, X-ray, MRI, CT scan interpretation (radiology). Each entry must include relevant keywords array and detailed markdown response content covering diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

requirements.summary: Update assistantBrain.ts routing logic to correctly identify and route user queries to the appropriate specialty handler for all 10 specialties, handling overlapping symptoms and falling back to general practitioner knowledge when no specific specialty is matched
acceptanceCriteria: Queries mentioning heart, chest pain, arrhythmia route to cardiology
Queries mentioning skin, rash, acne route to dermatology
Queries mentioning child, infant, vaccination route to pediatrics
Queries mentioning surgery, operation, wound route to surgery
Queries mentioning brain, nerve, seizure route to neurology
Queries mentioning cancer, tumor, chemotherapy route to oncology
Queries mentioning anesthesia, sedation, pain management route to anesthesiology
Queries mentioning pregnancy, menstruation, gynecology route to gynecology
Queries mentioning X-ray, MRI, scan, imaging route to radiology
Unmatched queries fall back to general practitioner responses

file_operations.description: Update the query routing logic to support all 10 medical specialties. Implement keyword matching against each specialty's keywords array from specialtyKnowledgeBase.ts. For overlapping symptoms, return the specialty with the highest keyword match score. Ensure queries route as follows: heart/chest pain/arrhythmia to cardiology; skin/rash/acne to dermatology; child/infant/vaccination to pediatrics; surgery/operation/wound to surgery; brain/nerve/seizure to neurology; cancer/tumor/chemotherapy to oncology; anesthesia/sedation/pain management to anesthesiology; pregnancy/menstruation to gynecology; X-ray/MRI/scan/imaging to radiology. Fall back to general practitioner knowledge when no specific specialty match is found. Do not break existing emergency detection logic.

requirements.summary: Update messageSummarizer.ts and responseFormatter.ts to ensure all assistant responses are presented in a concise, summarized format using bullet points and short paragraphs, covering diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and when to see a doctor
acceptanceCriteria: Assistant responses are structured with clear sections: Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, When to See a Doctor
Responses use bullet points and/or short paragraphs
Responses are concise and scannable, not long blocks of prose
Medical disclaimer is preserved in the formatted output

file_operations.description: Enhance the summarization logic to enforce structured, scannable output format. Ensure summarized responses are organized into four clear sections: (1) Diagnosis / What the condition is, (2) Treatment options, (3) Preventive measures, (4) When to see a doctor. Use bullet points for lists and short paragraphs for explanations. Preserve medical terminology and emergency indicators. Avoid long prose blocks.

Update response formatting to enforce the structured output format with clear section headers: Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, When to See a Doctor. Ensure responses use bullet points and short paragraphs for scannability. Preserve the medical disclaimer in all formatted output. Support the informational, urgent, reassuring, and general tones while maintaining the concise structure.

requirements.summary: Update Chat.tsx and AssistantPanel.tsx to display a specialty badge or label (e.g., '🫀 Cardiology', '🧠 Neurology') above or beside assistant response messages when a specific specialty knowledge base was used
acceptanceCriteria: A specialty badge/label appears on assistant messages that were generated from specialty knowledge
The badge reflects the correct specialty (e.g., Cardiology for heart-related queries)
General practitioner responses show a 'General Practice' badge
Badge is visually distinct and non-intrusive

file_operations.description: Extend the Message interface to include an optional 'specialty' field of type string that will store the detected specialty name (e.g., 'Cardiology', 'Neurology', 'General Practice') when a specialty knowledge base is used to generate the response.

Update the command processing logic to populate the 'specialty' field in the returned CommandResult when a specialty handler is invoked. Include the specialty name from specialtyKnowledgeBase.ts in the result metadata. For general practitioner fallback responses, set specialty to 'General Practice'.

Update the message rendering logic to display a specialty badge when message.specialty is present. Show the badge above or beside the assistant message content. Use emoji icons from the generated specialty-icons-set image (frontend/public/assets/generated/specialty-icons-set.dim_512x512.png) or Unicode emoji prefixes (e.g., 🫀 for Cardiology, 🧠 for Neurology, 🩺 for General Practice). Ensure the badge is visually distinct but non-intrusive, using subtle background color and small text size.

Update the message handling logic to extract and pass the specialty field from the CommandResult to the new Message object when adding assistant responses to the transcript. Ensure the specialty context is preserved and displayed when rendering messages in the full-page chat UI.

requirements.summary: Add a specialty selector UI element on the Chat page that allows users to optionally filter or direct their question to a specific medical specialty from the list of 10, with an 'Auto-detect' default option
acceptanceCriteria: A specialty dropdown or chip selector is visible on the Chat page
The selector lists all 10 specialties plus an 'Auto-detect' option
Selecting a specialty causes the assistant to use that specialty's knowledge base for the next response
The selected specialty is visually highlighted
'Auto-detect' is the default selection

file_operations.description: Add a new type 'SpecialtyFilter' as a union of specialty names ('cardiologist' | 'dermatologist' | 'pediatrician' | 'surgeon' | 'neurologist' | 'generalPractitioner' | 'anesthesiologist' | 'oncologist' | 'gynecologist' | 'radiologist' | 'autoDetect'). Export this type for use in the Chat page and assistant brain.

Update the processUserInput function signature to accept an optional 'specialtyFilter' parameter of type SpecialtyFilter. When a specific specialty is selected (not 'autoDetect'), bypass the keyword matching logic and route directly to the selected specialty's knowledge base. When 'autoDetect' is selected, use the existing keyword-based routing logic.

Add a specialty selector UI component above the message input area. Implement as a dropdown or horizontal chip selector listing all 10 specialties (Cardiology, Dermatology, Pediatrics, Surgery, Neurology, General Practice, Anesthesiology, Oncology, Gynecology, Radiology) plus an 'Auto-detect' option. Use icons from the generated specialty-icons-set image (frontend/public/assets/generated/specialty-icons-set.dim_512x512.png) or Unicode emoji. Manage the selected specialty in component state, defaulting to 'Auto-detect'. Pass the selected specialty filter to assistantBrain.processUserInput when handling user messages. Visually highlight the currently selected specialty.

Add the same specialty selector UI component to the assistant widget's chat interface, consistent with the full-page Chat experience. Manage selected specialty state and pass it to assistantBrain.processUserInput. Default to 'Auto-detect'.
